html_en:
The software factory is eating itself — in the best possible way. Today's feed is dominated by a single converging idea: autonomous agents aren't just tools anymore, they're the product, the infrastructure, and increasingly, the organization itself.

🏭 The Factory Is the Product

The most intellectually charged thread of the day comes from Guillermo Rauch, who is pushing a genuinely important reframe of how to think about software in the agent era.

"The (software) factory is the product. Your product is only as good as the agents you set up to autonomously maintain it. This is what @elonmusk figured out about Tesla, and it's now true for the software world." — @rauchg

He goes further, describing his own research workflow — no fancy apps, no knowledge graphs, just a research/ folder, an AGENTS.md file, and a CLI agent:

"The 'software' that powers this is English in AGENTS.md... If I want to share some outcome, I can ask the agent to render a cool HTML report and deploy it to Vercel. Scales to infinity." — @rauchg

@thenanyu adds a clever wrinkle: "The real reason we don't have a true SoftwareFactory" — gesturing at the recursive problem that if you can build a SoftwareFactory, you can build a SoftwareFactoryFactory. The abstraction goes all the way down, which is either the most exciting or most vertiginous thing you'll read today.

🤖 Agents in the Wild: Claude, Codex, and the Parallel QA Revolution

Some of the most concrete evidence that agentic workflows are maturing comes from practitioners actually running them at scale. Peter Steinberger shared a remarkable prompt he's been running against Codex for QA:

"Do a full end-to-end QA test of OpenClaw with live API keys. Use 12 subagents to split up functionality, spin up dev gateways with different ports, and use some to stress test. Orchestrate, use worktrees and create PRs autonomously. Set a goal to find 200 bugs. Fix the root cause each time, no band-aids." — @steipete
"Been running codex all day to do massive parallel QA in prep of the next release. Sol got insanely good at really understanding intent and is finding complex behavior issues. In the past such workflow did fell apart at compaction boundaries and/or the model started cheating." — @steipete

Meanwhile, @thsottiaux dropped a quietly significant milestone from inside OpenAI: "ChatGPT Work officially has overtaken Codex in number of active users." The agentic coding assistant is being eclipsed by broader workplace AI. The shift from "coding tool" to "work OS" is happening faster than most predicted.

Anthropic published two dense engineering pieces today. The Managed Agents architecture post explains how they decoupled the agent "brain" (Claude + harness) from the "hands" (sandboxes and tools) — borrowing the classic pets-vs-cattle analogy from infrastructure engineering. A companion product announcement adds self-hosted sandboxes and MCP tunnels, letting enterprise agents run entirely within a customer's own perimeter. Partners like Cloudflare, Vercel, Modal, and Daytona are already building on it.

🔧 Anthropic's Awkward Postmortem

Anthropic published a candid postmortem on Claude Code quality regressions that frustrated users over the past month. Three separate changes compounded into what looked like broad, mysterious degradation: a stealth downgrade of reasoning effort from high to medium, a caching bug that made Claude appear "forgetful," and a verbosity-reduction prompt that quietly hurt coding quality. None were intentional; all have been reverted.

The company is resetting usage limits for all subscribers as of April 23 — a goodwill gesture, but also an acknowledgment that trust, once eroded, needs active repair. The deeper lesson: as AI products grow more complex, silent regressions become existential trust problems, not just engineering bugs.

📊 The Hype Cycle, Examined Soberly

Watch/Listen: Ep 91: Top AI Analyst Unpacks Today's AI Hype Cycle — Unsupervised Learning

Benedict Evans joins Jacob Efron of Redpoint for a bracing dose of historical perspective. His core argument: before reaching for civilizational analogies, look at what actually happened the last five times transformative technology arrived.

"Nothing like this has ever happened before. And we've not had technology wiping out great swathes of jobs before... Yes, this is different, but it's always different." — Benedict Evans, Unsupervised Learning

His sharpest analogy is mobile networks: an industry that saw traffic grow 1,000–2,000x over fifteen years, spent $200B annually on CapEx, and still watched all the value accumulate elsewhere — to Uber, YouTube, banking apps. The infrastructure providers got commoditized. The open question, Evans argues, is whether foundation model labs are building the next Windows or the next fiber backbone.

"Sam Altman said, we're gonna be like Windows. But LLMs don't have network effects. So it doesn't look like they're gonna turn out like Windows." — Benedict Evans

🌍 Open Weights Has Won the Policy Argument (For Now)

Aaron Levie called it plainly after Google signed the open-weights AI letter:

"Now with Google on board, this is a complete endorsement of open weights AI. Pretty big moment for the industry." — @levie

@steipete added pointedly: "Proud that @OpenAI signed the letter. Ant is silent on it." Anthropic's absence from the signatories is conspicuous.

@realmadhuguru offered the most thoughtful framing for why consensus formed so quickly — and what it means for AI's bigger societal debates ahead:

"It took a series of public 'experiments' to play out. DeepSeek. Microsoft-OpenAI breakup. GLM. Kimi. Fable. The OpenAI-Hugging Face episode. Each revealed something different about incentives, innovation, geopolitics, and the cards the different players were holding... I think that's how we'll figure out many of AI's biggest societal questions over the next decade." — @realmadhuguru

In other words: reality is running the experiments so we don't have to argue from first principles forever. Small comfort, perhaps — but comfort nonetheless.
html_zh:
AI基础设施的竞争正在从模型能力转向部署架构——谁控制了"工厂"，谁就控制了未来。

🏭 软件工厂的哲学之争

本周最引人深思的讨论围绕一个核心隐喻展开：软件开发是否正在从"手工艺"转变为"工厂生产"？

Vercel创始人 Guillermo Rauch 给出了他的答案，语气不乏宣言意味：

"（软件）工厂本身才是产品。你的产品好坏取决于你设置的那些自主维护它的智能体。这正是 @elonmusk 在特斯拉身上悟透的道理，如今在软件世界同样成立。"

他进一步分享了自己的实际工作流——用一个 research/ 文件夹加一份 AGENTS.md 文档驱动所有研究：

"没有花哨的应用、知识图谱或UI。智能体可以被要求从过去的会话中查找和关联知识，无限扩展。驱动这一切的'软件'，就是写在 AGENTS.md 里的英文。"

但 @thenanyu 提出了一个更深刻的悖论：如果你能造出一个SoftwareFactory，你同样能造出一个SoftwareFactoryFactory——而这正是我们至今没有真正意义上的"软件工厂"的根本原因。递归的问题从未如此真实过。

🔧 Claude"变笨了"？Anthropic罕见公开复盘

Anthropic发布了一篇坦诚程度罕见的事后分析报告，承认过去一个月Claude Code的质量下滑源于三个独立的工程失误：

  • 3月4日：将Claude Code默认推理强度从"高"降至"中"，以减少卡顿感。结果引发大量用户投诉"模型变笨"，4月7日回滚。
  • 3月26日：一个旨在优化缓存的改动出现bug，导致Claude在每轮对话后都会"忘记"此前的推理过程，表现出前所未有的健忘症。
  • 4月16日：添加了一条"减少冗余输出"的系统提示，与其他改动叠加后严重损害了代码质量，4月20日回滚。

三个问题各自影响不同的用户群体、不同的时间段，叠加起来呈现出"广泛而无规律的退化"，令内部排查极为困难。Anthropic表示，截至4月23日，已为所有订阅用户重置使用额度。

这份报告的价值不仅在于解释了发生了什么，更在于它证明：即便是顶尖AI公司，也会在"让模型更快"与"让模型更聪明"之间做出错误的权衡取舍。

🏗️ Claude Managed Agents：把"大脑"和"双手"分开

Anthropic同日发布了两篇重量级工程博客，披露了其托管智能体架构的底层设计哲学。核心洞察来自一个经典的基础设施比喻：

"我们把智能体的各个组件虚拟化：会话（所有事件的只追加日志）、执行框架（调用Claude并路由工具调用的循环）、沙箱（Claude运行代码和编辑文件的执行环境）。这使得每个组件的底层实现可以自由替换，而不影响其他部分——就像操作系统的read()命令，无论底层是1970年代的磁盘还是现代SSD，上层接口始终稳定。"

简而言之：把"大脑"（Claude及其调度框架）与"双手"（沙箱和工具）彻底解耦。此前将所有组件塞进同一个容器的做法，使服务器成了"宠物"——一旦崩溃就要人工抢救。新架构让容器变成"牲口"：死了就换一头，会话状态独立保存，不受影响。

配套的新功能公告则将这一架构开放给企业：支持自托管沙箱（可接入Cloudflare、Vercel、Modal等）和私有网络MCP隧道，让智能体在企业防火墙内操作内部数据库和私有API，无需暴露任何公网端口。

🌍 开源权重：从争议到共识

当Google签署支持开放权重AI的公开信后，Box创始人 Aaron Levie 用一句话总结了这一时刻的分量：

"随着Google的加入，这份信成为了对开放权重AI的完整背书。对于整个行业而言，这是一个相当重要的时刻。"

@steipete 对OpenAI签署该信表示欢迎，同时不忘附上一句："Anthropic在这件事上沉默着。" 竞争立场，跃然纸上。

@realmadhuguru 则提供了一个更具历史感的视角：美国AI社区对开源权重的支持，是经由DeepSeek、微软与OpenAI的破裂、GLM、Kimi等一系列公开"实验"逐步形成的——

"在未知领域，对困难问题的答案只能来自与现实的反复接触……我们得以共同观察不同方向的一阶和二阶效应，并据此更新自己的判断。我认为，这就是未来十年我们解决AI最大社会问题的方式。"

📡 炒作周期中的冷静声音

Redpoint的Jacob Efron与分析师Benedict Evans的对谈（Watch/Listen: Unsupervised Learning Ep 91）提供了本周难得的降温时刻。Evans对"AI是有史以来最大技术革命"的论断保持审慎：

"我不觉得争论'这比移动互联网大还是比互联网大'有多大意义。更有价值的问题是：上五次出现颠覆性技术时发生了什么？……你可以指向移动通信——过去十五年流量增长了一两千倍，这是个万亿美元的行业，每年CapEx两千亿美元，但他们没做成Uber，没做成YouTube。所有价值都流向了上层。"

对于基础模型公司的终局价值，这个历史类比既是警告，也是路标。在今天ChatGPT Work用户数正式超越Codex的消息背后，谁是最终的价值捕获者，仍是悬而未决的问题。
